merge.reason: Same weekly business review. ORCH-C06 is an empty stub; LOOP-C01 has the full record. Renumber LOOP-C01 into the ORCH namespace when merged.

One dated seasonal calendar. ORCH-C09 is an empty stub of LOOP-C05. MONEY-C19 (acquisition financial calendar and peak guardrails) repeats LOOP-C05's base and stretch budget gates per window. BRAND-C65 (festive moment calendar for PR and events) is the same dated calendar; BRAND reads it and adds PR moments as rows.
Same crisis protocol. ORCH-C10 is an empty stub; LOOP-C06 has the full record.
BRN-C13 (Door B first full build) is just the first run of BRN-C01, C02 and C04, invoked by ORCH-C08's onboarding run. One onboarding capability; the brain build is a step inside it.

One pre-delivery QA gate owned by QA. QA-C02 (check specialist artefacts) and QA-C03 (check reports) are the same gate as LOOP-C12. SITE-C34, CREA-C14, BRAND-C38, ORG-C15 and LIFE-C21 are per-surface copies of the same claims and honesty check; they become surface checklists inside the gate plus a self-check in each specialist's output contract, not separate capabilities. Fold claims-tier tracing (from QA-C02) into LOOP-C12's encompasses.

Claim tiering has one owner, the Keeper (ARCHITECTURE: Keeper tiers claims). QA-C04 (tier new claims found in artefacts, route to founder) and BRAND-C22 (verify first/only/number-one and comparison claims against evidence and legal risk) both produce a claims-tier entry.

One decision log owned by the Registrar. REG-C01 is an empty stub of LOOP-C10. MONEY-C40 (log every high-stakes decision with metric and review date) is the same log; its bottleneck-diagnosis part is DIAG's.
Both surface reads due and stale decisions. The Registrar owns read points and staleness; delivery goes through the Today screen (ORCH-C01), so ORCH-C11 is not a separate capability.
Taking a read at a read point with the control comparison in code is the Registrar's job for every registry entry, wild bets included.
REG-C07 (the brand's memory list: what was tried, what it did) is a view over the results REG-C03 records. Same output.

One ranker. PROP-C04 is an empty stub of LOOP-C09. SITE-C49 (score and prioritise the CRO backlog by expected profit) is a second ranker; SITE supplies hypotheses and evidence via the surface audit and Propose ranks them with everything else.

Answering a founder question is one capability. ORCH-C12 (explain any part of the business) duplicates ORCH-C04. MONEY-C62 (ask-the-data analyst over the metric contract) is the same Q&A with metric-read as a skill.

Both take facts, decisions and actions out of a conversation and route them to the brain, the decision log and queues. ORCH-C05 (chat) is an empty stub; LOOP-C19 has the full routing logic. Make the input 'chat or transcript'.
Both are the founder gate delivered on mobile while away (WhatsApp reply vs voice-note brief). One capability: mobile approvals, with voice or text summary.

Hand-offs and escalation are routing, not capabilities (README: hand-offs are named in agent files). SITE-C20 routes out-of-scope findings, MEDIA-C48 routes founder calls, PROD-C25 hands hiring to MONEY, PROD-C26 hands cash signals to MONEY. None has its own output type.

The metric contract has one owner. ARCHITECTURE puts computation and freshness in the data layer (Keeper). MONEY-C25 (maintain metric contract and revenue definitions) is the same artefact; MONEY advises on definitions as an input.

Landing sources on a schedule with freshness and failure flags is the Keeper's collector job. MONEY-C61 (warehouse and ETL) and MONEY-C26 (daily pass/warn/fail trust check) are the same collector run and its post-check.

Analytics setup and audit sits with measurement (06-MEA, MONEY). SITE-C17 (install tracking, UTM rules) and ORG-C31 (GA4, Search Console, GTM setup) are the same GA4 setup. The founder morning report part of SITE-C17 is already MONEY-C14 and LOOP-C01.
Same Meta pixel and CAPI event-health audit. Tracking is measurement (MONEY). MEDIA reads the result before kill or scale calls.
Platform ROAS vs blended MER is one of the attribution-model gaps MONEY-C23 reports. One reconciliation, read by MEDIA through the metric-read skill.

CAC, payback and LTGP:CAC is one finance output. LIFE-C31 computes LTGP and CAC targets; MEDIA-C08 builds the new-customer P&L and sets ROAS/CPA targets from margin. Same numbers, three owners. MEDIA and LIFE read the targets.
RFM and cohort segmentation is the segment model the flows use. LIFE-C12 already scores RFM against the brand's own base.
Funnel diagnosis and revenue triage (sessions x CR x AOV) are the pipeline break read, which is DIAG's. MONEY keeps the numbers, not the diagnosis.
Ad-platform invoices against spend and the budget ledger are one of the platform-to-books gaps. MEDIA-C66 is the automated mode of MEDIA-C57; both are accounting output, owned by MONEY.
Same three-way PO, receipt and invoice match. Accounts payable is MONEY's; PROD supplies the PO and receipt.

COD remittance reconciliation is one cash job. PROD-C57 repeats it; MONEY-C79 (draft the escalation email) is the next step of the same capability and brings its founder_gate for the send. Courier weight-billing disputes move to PROD-C67.
MONEY-C80 is the live mode of MONEY-C08's financing comparison against the same 13-week forecast.
Both build the voice sheet from liked and disliked examples. BRAND owns voice (04-BRD); the Keeper stores it.

One verbatim language bank per avatar. BRN-C10 maintains the avatar and language bank 'with the Brand strategist'; CREA-C01 mines reviews, tickets and search terms into a research packet. Same sources, same output. CREA pulls a packet from BRAND-C14.
Buyer personas and the avatar record are the same artefact. BRAND owns avatars (02-AVT).

BRAND-C50 (keep identity and customer sections current) duplicates BRAND-C15 (maintain and refresh avatars) plus BRAND-C32 and BRN-C03. Storage is the Keeper's; content comes from the owning BRAND capabilities.
Both produce a ranked list of ad angles with proof per persona. Angles are creative output; CREA owns them and reads the avatar record.
Same voice-of-customer program (surveys, interviews, polls). CX (17-CXP) owns NPS/CSAT and VoC; BRAND-C05 keeps discovery interviews.

Competitor collection is one data-layer job. BRAND-C56 (continuous monitoring with change alerts), LIFE-C56 (competitor prices), LIFE-C63 (competitor policy pages), MEDIA-C43 (competitor ads, pricing, keywords) and ORG-C50 (weekly competitor change brief) all snapshot the same public sources on a schedule. Specialists subscribe to the Keeper's alerts; MEDIA's reaction rule (pull a shared SKU on a 20-30% competitor discount) becomes a MEDIA-C17 input. ORG-C50's AI-answer part stays in ORG-C37.
One competitor teardown standard owned by the Scout. SCT-C03 (tag competitor ads and pages as signals) and CREA-C33 (research competitor creative, signal only) are teardowns in the same shape.

Three records for marketplace MAP and price parity. PROD-C46 (Buy Box, reseller pricing, MAP), LIFE-C57 (MAP and parity) and LOOP-C30 (listing parity and unauthorised resellers) produce the same flags. Marketplaces are PROD's (22-AMZ); the Keeper's crawl can feed it.

Three audits of ad-to-page match. SITE-C36 covers ad to page to checkout; CREA-C53 checks live ads vs destination; MEDIA-C44 mirrors the best headline on the landing page. One audit, owned by SITE because the fix usually lands on the page.
Landing and product page copy blocks are page copy. ARCHITECTURE gives page specs and copy to SITE. CREA supplies the ad promise as an input.
Both decide where ad traffic lands (PDP, advertorial, quiz, marketplace, shared offer). Funnel architecture is SITE's output.

Email and SMS copy is Lifecycle's (ARCHITECTURE: Lifecycle produces flows and campaigns). CREA-C30 writes lifecycle email copy blocks; CREA-C29 writes SMS marketing copy. LIFE-C14 already covers both channels.
Marketplace listing copy is part of the listing, which PROD produces (ARCHITECTURE). Same title and bullet rules.
Both draft the Amazon PPC structure as a change list; PROD-C37 already hands execution to MEDIA. Ads are MEDIA's.
Same Product, Offer, Review, Breadcrumb and FAQ schema on money pages. Structured data is technical SEO (15-SEO, ORG).
Both design the collection tree and menu. Store information architecture is SITE's; ORG adds URL and doorway-page rules as an SEO input.
Both design quizzes and on-site personalization with lift vs non-quiz buyers. The output is a site change.
Both set on-site search and merchandising ranking rules. The surface is the site.
One master product feed. ORG-C30 keeps the merchant feed accurate for free listings and AI shopping, which is PROD-C47's feed handed to ORG.
CREA-C23 (flag DPA template and feed risks) is the QA step of CREA-C52 (design DPA overlay templates). Same artefact.
Offer construction is Lifecycle's (03-OFF). CREA-C13 writes bundle, guarantee, urgency and value stack 'as a lever'; that is LIFE-C36, C39 and C42's job. CREA writes ad copy about the approved offer.
SITE-C41 designs bundle tiers and savings per tier, which is LIFE-C39. The page layout of the buy box stays in SITE-C38.
Same margin waterfall and break-even go/no-go for an offer or promo. The economics model is finance output (MONEY).
Both design the pop-up offer; LIFE-C44's economics is the MONEY-C05 model applied to it.
Both design referral incentives. Referral programs are an offer (LIFE); packaging and unboxing parts of BRAND-C43 are LIFE-C25.
LIFE-C61 (personalised win-back per lapsed customer) is a mode of the win-back flow, not a separate job. Keep its founder_gate for the send.
Same cross-channel allocation by marginal return. Cross-domain allocation is ORCH's; MEDIA reports each channel's headroom.
MEDIA-C64 (autonomous budget agent in guardrails) is the continuous mode of MEDIA-C63's standing rules. The cross-channel part belongs to LOOP-C03.
Both govern platform-native automation (suggestions, Advantage+, PMax auto features) with a log and guardrails.
MEDIA-C65 (policy pre-check from rejection history) is the prevention step of MEDIA-C55 (track and resolve policy rejections). One ad-policy capability.
Both set up creative test structure, winner rule and read window in the ad account. Test plans and kill rules are MEDIA's (ARCHITECTURE); CREA supplies hypotheses.
One creative volume and production plan. MEDIA-C16 sets ads per $1,000 and concept counts; CREA-C50 is the festive version of the same production calendar, fed by LOOP-C05.
Both diagnose creative fatigue (frequency by segment vs persona pool) and fix the creative mix. The artefact is a revival plan, which CREA owns; frequency is a metric-read input.
CREA-C20 keeps the live platform-spec sheet; MEDIA-C28 checks TikTok videos against the same spec.
CREA-C34 (line edit and readability in code before QA) is the self-check of CREA-C26 (apply the copy rules). Same procedure.
Same AI-use policy (AI drafts, a human originates and fact-checks). One policy for all written output.
Both scan public posts for creators already using the brand or category and draft outreach. One discovery agent; MEDIA picks whitelisting candidates from its list.
The COD confirmation flow on WhatsApp is LIFE-C22's (and SITE-C67 triggers it). Click-to-WhatsApp ads are a campaign type under MEDIA-C09 and C11, not a separate capability.

Three records for reputation-crisis response (detect a public complaint, draft a holding statement and channel plan). The public statement is PR output (BRAND). ORG posts it; LOOP-C06 runs the cross-team crisis.
Review requests and responses are one program across the site, Google and marketplaces. PROD-C38 keeps marketplace account health.
Both set up and moderate an owned customer community (Slack, Discord, Circle, WhatsApp). A customer community is a retention program (LIFE).
Support macros and knowledge base are CX output (17-CXP). MONEY-C38 keeps capacity planning.
ORG-C51 says it 'extends ORG-C47'. Same feedback loop; keep one record with founder_gate on the ticket step.
Three NDR records. LIFE-C64 (reschedule via courier portal) is an execution route; PROD-C76 (reschedule vs RTO by unit economics) is the decision rule. Both sit inside NDR resolution.
Both change checkout payment options for COD-heavy pincodes (prepaid-only, partial advance, COD fee). The surface is checkout (SITE).
Supplier contracts, price locks and renewal dates are the same dated contract register the Keeper holds.
PROD-C09 turns specs into a sourcing request suppliers quote on, which is the RFQ (PROD-C15). Supplier vetting in it is PROD-C14.
PROD-C33 repeats sample sign-off and pre-shipment inspection for FBA runs. FNSKU labelling goes to PROD-C35.
Tracking sample shipments from several factories is part of the sample gate.
PROD-C75 (agent-led negotiation in guardrails) is a mode of the cost-down negotiation. Keep its founder_gate.
Both watch lookalike domains, squatting and counterfeit listings. Keep one watch in security (23-SEC) and add BRAND-C69's trademark, domain and handle renewal dates to it.
Both keep a live inventory of every app, script and tag, vet before install and remove unused ones. One inventory; the CVE and dependency scan is a step MONEY-C50's security audit reads.
Both draft a periodic founder update from the registry with numbers, what worked and what did not. One update; BRAND supplies the brand narrative section.

reassign.reason: A launch plan that sequences several specialists with dates is process and routing, which ORCH owns. PROP ranks ideas; it does not run cross-team timelines (compare LOOP-C16, owned by ORCH).
Fanning an anomaly out to site speed, stock and competitor data for root cause is a cross-domain diagnosis. DIAG owns root cause across stages.
Conversion tracking setup (primary action, enhanced conversions, GTM or server route) is measurement (06-MEA). This keeps it with MONEY-C20 and C21.
Choosing and setting up an attribution or MMM tool is measurement stack work. It sits next to MONEY-C23 and MONEY-C63.
Partnership Ads and Spark authorisation is ad-account setup, like MEDIA-C26's Spark codes. CREA owns the asset, not the ad account.
GST credit notes against refunds are accounting and tax (MONEY-C12). The output is a filing, not a customer message.
DPDP access and erasure requests across every system are privacy compliance, which MONEY-C49 owns. LIFE hands the request in from support.
True customer profitability (support, returns, shipping and discount cost per customer) is a margin model. MONEY computes it; LIFE uses it for tiers.
The 'how did you hear about us' survey is an attribution input to the measurement stack, next to MONEY-C23.
Identity resolution across orders, ESP, WhatsApp, POS and marketplaces is data-layer work. It sits with the collectors and warehouse (BRN-C02), and every specialist reads it.
Daily 3PL and warehouse SLA tracking is physical fulfilment. PROD already owns 3PL selection (PROD-C52), warehouse workflow (PROD-C53) and courier scorecards (PROD-C59).
Gating POs on a tech pack and running the production critical path is sourcing work (PROD-C13, C16, C70). MONEY keeps the cash side (MONEY-C07).
ARCHITECTURE gives landed cost models to Product and supply (skill landed-cost-model), and PROD-C23 already refreshes landed cost. MONEY reads it for margin.
Drafting a courier or 3PL rate renegotiation is logistics vendor work, next to PROD-C59 courier scorecards. The Keeper holds facts; it should not write outbound asks.
HSN/SAC mapping and e-invoice rejections are GST compliance (MONEY-C12). PROD supplies the SKU master.
A mystery-shopper walk of browse, checkout, confirmation and a real support query is a customer-experience audit (17-CXP). It is not brand strategy.
Setting paid budget and a CPA ceiling for existing customers is paid media. MEDIA-C19 already holds all existing-customer spend in one campaign.
Crowdfunding, private capital and financing options are MONEY-C08's job. The 'hard-to-source manufacturer' part can stay a PROD-C14 note.

What AI shopping agents say about the brand is the same surface as ORG-C37 (AI visibility) and ORG-C36 (correct wrong AI facts). QA keeps the claims-tier check through LOOP-C12. The agent-assisted performance note is a channel read, not a QA pass.
Reconciling what the affiliate network says is owed against real orders is a payout reconciliation. MEDIA keeps commission design; MONEY reconciles and pays.
Recomputing quick-commerce ROAS from transaction value (not MRP) is an ad-performance read for MEDIA-C53's retail media. Dark-store unit economics can stay a PROD note.

gaps.name: On-site AI shopping assistant
gaps.what: A pre-purchase chat on the site that answers product, size and delivery questions from the catalogue, stock and claims tiers only, and hands off to a person. Different from LIFE-C49 (support actions) and SITE-C73 (third-party agents).
gaps.trigger: event: founder approves; weekly transcript and claims review

gaps.name: Chargeback and payment dispute responses
gaps.what: Build the evidence pack (order, delivery proof, OTP, chat log) for each gateway chargeback or UPI dispute and file it before the deadline. Track win rate by reason code. MONEY-C42 sets alert thresholds but nothing answers disputes.
gaps.trigger: event: dispute opened on a payment gateway

gaps.name: Courier lost and damaged parcel claims
gaps.what: File claims with couriers and aggregators for lost, damaged or wrongly marked RTO shipments, with proof, and track payout against the claim. Only FBA paperwork (PROD-C35) is covered today.
gaps.trigger: event: shipment marked lost or damaged, or RTO received damaged; weekly sweep

gaps.name: Marketplace reimbursement claims
gaps.what: Find and file reimbursements for lost or damaged marketplace inventory and wrong fees (FBA reimbursements, Flipkart SPF, Myntra claims) inside each seller console.
gaps.trigger: weekly

gaps.name: Insurance claims
gaps.what: Prepare and track claims under transit, stock, cyber and product liability policies, with the evidence each insurer asks for. MONEY-C59 buys cover but nothing files claims.
gaps.trigger: event: insured loss

gaps.name: Influencer agreements and ASCI disclosure checks
gaps.what: Keep a creator agreement template (deliverables, usage rights, exclusivity, payment, disclosure clause) and check live creator and affiliate posts carry the ASCI and platform disclosure. CREA-C10 tracks rights but no contract or live disclosure check exists.
gaps.trigger: event: creator deal agreed; weekly check of live posts

gaps.name: Shoot production and model releases
gaps.what: Run the shoot: shot list, call sheet, studio or location and model booking, signed model and location releases, retouch QA against the real product, and filing to the asset library. CREA-C12 directs photos; ORG-C06 covers organic batching only.
gaps.trigger: event: shoot approved

gaps.name: Packaging artwork and mandatory label brief
gaps.what: Brief packaging artwork and dielines per channel with mandatory declarations placed (MRP, Legal Metrology, net quantity, BIS or hallmark, EPR mark). PROD-C13 has the spec and LIFE-C25 the unboxing, but no one owns the artwork.
gaps.trigger: event: new SKU, new channel or packaging change

gaps.name: Festive gifting operations
gaps.what: Turn on gift wrap, gift message, price-hidden gift invoice and delivery-by-date cutoffs per pincode for Diwali, Rakhi and wedding season, plus gift guides, and switch them off after the window.
gaps.trigger: event: 60 days before each gifting window in LOOP-C05

gaps.name: Corporate gifting sales desk
gaps.what: Run B2B gifting orders: lead list, quote with bulk tiers, custom packaging or engraving, GST invoice, split delivery to many addresses, and a repeat-order reminder next season. LIFE-C58 has corporate gift card terms only.
gaps.trigger: event: inbound corporate enquiry; 90 days before Diwali for outbound

gaps.name: Offline retail, stockist and pop-up operations
gaps.what: Run the operations of a pop-up, exhibition or stockist: POS setup, stock transfer and return, consignment settlement, staff roster and daily sales reconciliation into the metric contract. BRAND-C42 only designs the event.
gaps.trigger: event: pop-up, exhibition or stockist deal approved

gaps.name: Subscription payment failure recovery
gaps.what: Set retry schedules, card-updater and UPI AutoPay or e-mandate re-authorisation (RBI rules) for failed renewals, and measure involuntary churn apart from cancellations. LIFE-C09 sends the message but no one owns the recovery setup.
gaps.trigger: event: failed renewal; monthly involuntary-churn read

gaps.name: Mobile app operations (if the brand has an app)
gaps.what: App store listing and screenshots, release QA, deep links from ads and email, push opt-in prompt and app-only offers, and app ratings. No record covers an app.
gaps.trigger: event: brand has or launches an app; per release

gaps.name: Export compliance and international duties
gaps.what: Set up IEC and LUT for zero-rated exports, HS codes, commercial invoice and courier export paperwork, and choose DDP vs DDU so the buyer is not surprised by duty. SITE-C12 and PROD-C21 do not cover the paperwork.
gaps.trigger: event: first international order or new export market

gaps.name: Multi-channel inventory sync and order routing
gaps.what: Keep one stock pool across site, marketplaces, quick commerce and stores, with per-channel buffers to stop overselling, and set order routing and split-shipment rules. PROD-C63 only audits mismatches after the fact.
gaps.trigger: continuous; event: new channel added

gaps.name: GST return preparation and e-way bills
gaps.what: Prepare GSTR-1 and 3B, match input credit against GSTR-2B, claim marketplace TCS and TDS credits, and raise e-way bills for B2B and stock transfers. MONEY-C12 tracks thresholds only.
gaps.trigger: monthly; event: B2B dispatch or stock transfer

gaps.name: Month-end close and management accounts
gaps.what: Run a close checklist (bank and gateway recs, accruals, inventory valuation, deferred revenue) and publish management accounts against budget. The pieces exist (MONEY-C51, C53, C56), but nothing owns the close.
gaps.trigger: monthly

gaps.name: Product recall and safety incident procedure
gaps.what: When a defect is a safety risk, find affected batches, stop sale on every channel, contact buyers, arrange returns or replacements, and log regulator notices. PROD-C73 covers CAPA only, and LOOP-C06 is generic.
gaps.trigger: event: safety-related defect or regulator notice

gaps.name: Grievance officer queue and consumer notices
gaps.what: Run the grievance queue required by India's E-Commerce Rules: acknowledge in 48 hours and resolve in 1 month. Track consumer-forum (e-Daakhil) and legal notices to closure. LOOP-C27 checks the disclosure but nobody works the queue.
gaps.trigger: event: grievance or notice received; weekly SLA check

gaps.name: Warranty, repair and after-sales service
gaps.what: Run resizing, repair, re-plating, warranty and buyback or exchange requests. That means intake, courier pickup, repair partner, status updates and cost per case. This matters for jewellery and durable goods, and returns (LIFE-C26) do not cover it.
gaps.trigger: event: service request

gaps.name: Made-to-order and personalised order workflow
gaps.what: Handle engraving, custom size or made-to-order items: capture the spec at checkout, get the customer's approval on a proof, track production, and state non-returnable terms. No record covers custom orders.
gaps.trigger: event: personalised or made-to-order SKU sold

autonomy.reason: Builds live ESP flows that email customers (back-in-stock, review request). external_write=ESP flow build and customer-facing.
Writes segments into the ESP (external_write=ESP segment build). Segments decide who gets every send.
Writes templates into the ESP (external_write=ESP template build). The template is what customers see.
Changes DNS and suppression settings on the ESP. A wrong suppression silently stops or restarts mail to real customers.
Sends NPS and CSAT surveys to customers (external_write=survey tool send).
Adds a survey to the live thank-you page (external_write=storefront). Customer-facing.
Pushes reviews and UGC into the product feed, ads and marketplace listings. External write, customer-facing, and needs usage rights.
Merges guest-checkout orders into accounts. That is a write to customer records in the store and ESP and is hard to undo.
Refreshes, redirects and prunes live pages (external_write=site pages / redirect rules). Changes what customers and search engines see.
Edits live page content to add links (external_write=site page content).
Picks and fails over couriers through the aggregator API. An external write that changes shipping spend and delivery for real orders.
Moves shipping volume by changing aggregator courier priority settings. External write that changes spend.
Pushes the feed to channels (outputs include a per-channel push log). Prices and stock shown to customers change.
Runs Amazon coupons, Lightning Deals and Prime Day promotions. That spends margin and changes customer-facing price.
The steps include sending forecasts and PO drafts to suppliers, flagging SKUs on the PDP and throttling ad spend. Keep the compute as agent_does; gate the send, PDP and spend steps.
Turning off auto-apply and testing suggestions in a sandbox are ad-account writes. Meta is read-only, so the output is a change list for a person.
Capping the DPA ad set and moving it out of the cold CBO are ad-account changes. The output is a change list.
Throttling spend and running clearance or new-arrival campaigns are budget changes. Meta is read-only, so it produces a change list.

'Configure' GA4 means changing retention, events, filters and Signals, with 'settings change log entries' as output. That is an external write, and the Signals and consent change needs a founder decision.
Fixing link mismatches means editing live ad, email and social URLs. Those are external writes (Meta is read-only).
Locking the registrar account and fixing dangling DNS records need a person with the registrar login. It is a write.
Posts journal entries to the accounting ledger (external_write=accounting ledger). An accountant should import and post.
Writes depreciation entries to the accounting ledger.
Writes expense and card reconciliations to the ledger and applies expense policy to staff claims.
Writes FX conversions and payment reconciliations to the ledger.
'Ships a winner' changes the live site for every customer. It needs a founder decision, even after a test win.
Fixes broken links, changes redirects and reconciles platform inventory on the live store. Those writes change what customers see and what can be bought.
Approves ambassadors, assigns tasks and may pay rewards on an external platform (external_write flagged). Customer-facing and may spend money.
Places a real purchase (spends money) and opens a real support ticket (uses team time). external_write is already flagged 'founder-approved', which conflicts with agent_does.
Spends on licensed AI-actor generation. A synthetic person reading a hook to camera can read as an invented testimonial, which touches the no-invented-people red line.
